actors.scope: arguments to public methods only: fixture_facts (legacy only), captures/admission_ref/runtime kwargs to authorize_capture_set, any externally held reference to a previously returned snapshot/anchor/graph-token object
actors.explicitly_out_of_scope: direct mutation of module globals, monkeypatching classes/methods, reassignment of _P4_* dispatch pins, reflection-based tampering with _records/__slots__ state — these require interpreter code-execution privilege, which implementation-workflow.md point 4 states is NOT an external security boundary ('Mutable Python internals are not an external security boundary'). The _p4_fixed_integrity/_p4_snapshot_integrity self-checks that defend against exactly this remain in place as defense-in-depth/regression detectors, not as the modeled external boundary, matching how ADR-0141/0142 scoped WORM/process-local trust.

authority_boundary_statement: Per docs/skills/implementation-workflow.md point 4 and consistent with ADR-0141 Decision point 5 ('nonauthorizing... Process-local WORM immutability after proof is a trusted-host invariant; hostile interpreter code is outside this nondeployment contract') and ADR-0142 Decision point 2 ('Process-local WORM immutability after proof is a trusted-host invariant'): this matrix treats hostile DATA (fixture_facts, captures, admission_ref, runtime, stale/foreign token objects reachable through the public API) as adversarial, and treats the trusted host's SQLite reserve file and Python process/interpreter as non-adversarial. A narrowed threat model beyond this would need owner approval; this matrix does not narrow anything ADR-0141/0142/0143 already scoped.

class_function_inventory.slots_pin: __slots__ = ('_graph', '_snapshot', '_terminal', '__weakref__') — Phase 0 pin: NO '_records' slot (unlike the legacy resolver); this resolver never caches artifact bytes, it always re-derives through graph.snapshot()/graph.resolve() per call (Decision point 2)
class_function_inventory.methods: snapshot(), resolve(snapshot, exact_ref_bytes), _checked_resolve(snapshot, exact_ref_bytes), close_admission(snapshot, admission_ref, live_projection) — identical four-method contract, no _lookup method (Decision point 1)

class_function_inventory.name: _DynamicP4TerminalArtifactVerifier(TerminalArtifactVerifier)
class_function_inventory.final_marker: __new__ raises TypeError, __init_subclass__ raises TypeError, __slots__ = () — exact mirror of _FixedTerminalArtifactVerifier (Decision point 5)
class_function_inventory.methods: verify_terminal(...), require_current(...) registered only against the dynamic resolver's own snapshot/12-ref corpus, never _P4_EXTERNAL_RECORDS; keyring reuses _P4_LOCAL_PUBLIC_KEYS (no new key material)

class_function_inventory.name: _DynamicP4VerificationClock(TrustedClock)
class_function_inventory.pin: now_ms() returns reserve._now() read under the resolver's own held read transaction (Decision point 6). Phase 0 must pin construction shape: __init__(reserve) storing a frozen reference (object.__setattr__), and must pin that now_ms() is only ever called from inside a transaction the resolver already opened — mirroring NonAuthorizingDynamicRootGraph._vector's own `_hs_refuse(not connection.in_transaction, ...)` guard (trust.py:8893), inverted: now_ms() called OUTSIDE a held transaction must refuse, not silently open its own.

class_function_inventory.name: _DynamicP4VerificationRevocations(HistoricalStudyRevocations)
class_function_inventory.pin: is_unrevoked(snapshot_sha256, key_id, key_version, now_ms) checks the live reserve._snapshot() digest (never the fixed literal or _digest(b"p4-fixed-revocations")); key_id checked against the same _P4_LOCAL_PUBLIC_KEYS set the dynamic terminal verifier uses. Phase 0 must pin: now_ms is compared for exact equality to the value read inside the SAME guarded transaction as snapshot_sha256 (no TOCTOU window between reading now_ms and reading the revocation digest) — unlike the legacy class's hardcoded now_ms==500, this one has a live value that can change between two separate unguarded reads.

class_function_inventory.name: _development_dynamic_p4_broker(issuer)
class_function_inventory.pin: consumes fresh _P4_PENDING_DYNAMIC_TOKENS set (mirrors _P4_PENDING_TOKENS, never the legacy set); constructs _DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver from issuer.graph(), then a second instance of the unmodified _SyntheticP4CapturedAuthorizationAuthority via its existing __init__(token, resolver) (Decision point 3); spends one reserve_uses(kind='dynamic-p4-authority') row before returning (Decision point 9).
class_function_inventory.ordering_not_frozen_by_adr_phase0_must_p: the ADR text does not state whether the reserve_uses spend happens BEFORE or AFTER constructing the resolver/terminal/clock/revocations objects. This matrix recommends and Phase 0 must pin: RESERVE FIRST. Concretely: (1) read the root-pis row for the pair, assert state=ISSUED, derive signed_id per Decision point 9; (2) BEGIN IMMEDIATE, recheck ISSUED, INSERT the RESERVED row + audit, UPDATE to ISSUED + audit, COMMIT (mirrors _SyntheticRootPisIssuer.issue's own RESERVED->ISSUED-in-one-transaction shape at trust.py:8409-8435); (3) only then construct the resolver/terminal/clock/revocations/authority objects; (4) any failure between the reserve COMMIT and a successful return quarantines the row (new helper mirroring _SyntheticRootPisIssuer._quarantine at trust.py:8219, not specified by the ADR text and must be authored in Phase 0). Reserve-after would let two racing callers each build a full resolver+terminal+authority object before either one's reserve spend collides — see matrix row 11.

class_function_inventory.name: _p4_require_issued_authority(authority)
class_function_inventory.current_shape_pin: today (trust.py:2473-2489) is ONE `if (...)` block with 8 OR-ed clauses all raising the same TypeError. Two of those clauses are resolver-type-specific and CANNOT simply gain an elif: `type(issued[0]) is not _FixedWormTrustedArtifactResolver` and `type(issued[0])._lookup is not _P4_RESOLVER_LOOKUP` (the dynamic resolver has no _lookup method at all, per Decision point 1's four-method contract). Phase 0 must pin the exact split: authority/ledger-identity clauses (`issued is None`, `authority._p4_resolver is not issued[0]`, `CapturedAuthorizationAuthority.authorize_capture_set is not _P4_BASE_DISPATCH`, `type(authority).authorize_capture_set is not _P4_FINAL_DISPATCH`, `type(authority)._validate_capture_request is not _P4_REQUEST_CHECK`, `"authorize_capture_set" in authority.__dict__`) stay as shared pre-checks before the if/elif/else (both authority instances use the identical final class); the two resolver-type-specific clauses move one-for-one into their matching branch, and the dynamic elif branch pins an analogous but distinct method-identity check in place of `_lookup` — e.g. `type(issued[0]).resolve is _P4_DYNAMIC_RESOLVER_LOOKUP` (exact name TBD, Phase 0 deliverable).

class_function_inventory.name: _p4_snapshot_integrity(resolver, snapshot)
class_function_inventory.current_shape_pin: today (trust.py:4195-4221) unconditionally calls _p4_fixed_integrity() FIRST (line 4199), before the resolver-type check. _p4_fixed_integrity pins ONLY legacy-fixed globals (legacy _p4_close_admission identity, the legacy _P4_VERIFICATION keyring/clock/revocations pin, the shared _P4_SHAPES/_P4_ARTIFACT_SPECS digest). Decision point 4's quoted if/elif/else text for this function does not mention this call. Phase 0 must pin whether: (a) _p4_fixed_integrity() keeps running unconditionally for both branches (harmless but asymmetric — it defends legacy dispatch identity but nothing analogous defends the dynamic branch's own new pins), or (b) a new _p4_dynamic_fixed_integrity() is added and called from the elif branch, pinning `_dynamic_p4_close_admission is <its own module-level pin>`, `type(clock).now_ms is <pinned>`, `type(revocations).is_unrevoked is <pinned>`, and `(verify_terminal, require_current)` identity for _DynamicP4TerminalArtifactVerifier (mirroring _P4_TERMINAL_METHODS). See open finding F1 below — this matrix recommends (b).

class_function_inventory.name: _dynamic_p4_close_admission(resolver, snapshot, admission_ref, live_projection)
class_function_inventory.pin: new closure-walk function mirroring _p4_close_admission's visit/find/get recursion shape (Decision point 7), sized only to root-capture-admission -> cas -> pce; bound at module scope as e.g. _P4_DYNAMIC_CLOSE_ADMISSION = _dynamic_p4_close_admission (exact name is a Phase 0 deliverable) and referenced only from _DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver.close_admission; _p4_close_admission/_P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION are never modified, called, or reachable from this path (Decision point 4 last sentence).

dskit/production/verifier.py: HistoricalStudyVerifier.authorize_capture_set (line 857) IS a facade this ADR touches transitively. Grep-verified (F4, resolved): it does NOT import or re-export _development_p4_broker, _SyntheticP4CapturedAuthorizationAuthority, or any resolver class by name; instead it holds a generic self._authority pinned at construction (_P4_VERIFIER_PINS) and dispatches through `isinstance(authority, CapturedAuthorizationAuthority)` (line 902) plus a fixed-dispatch-identity pin (line 904), never an exact-type check against the legacy or dynamic authority class. Whichever authority instance (legacy or dynamic) a caller binds into a HistoricalStudyVerifier, this facade forwards to it transparently, so its safety here depends ENTIRELY on _p4_require_issued_authority/_p4_snapshot_integrity's own dispatch correctness deeper in the call (matrix rows 1-2), not on anything in verifier.py itself. No edit to verifier.py is implied by this ADR; it is listed as a facade because it is a second public entry point that reaches the same gated authorize_capture_set path.

matrix.family: dynamic-p4-authority reserve row constructed before root-pis reaches ISSUED
cases: attempt to derive/reserve the dynamic-p4-authority signed_id while the root-pis row for that pair is still RESERVED (not yet ISSUED)
attempt against a root-pis row that is QUARANTINED
attempt against a signed_id pair with NO root-pis row at all (never reserved)
race: root-pis issuance and dynamic-p4-authority reservation attempted concurrently by two callers, one still mid-transaction

matrix.forbidden_effect: a dynamic-p4-authority row reaching ISSUED (or even RESERVED) while its preimage root-pis row is not ISSUED at the moment of that same transaction's read

matrix.family: second construction attempt for the same derived signed_id
cases: call _development_dynamic_p4_broker(issuer) twice with the SAME issuer after the first call already reached ISSUED

call it with a DIFFERENT _SyntheticRootPisIssuer instance that happens to be a fresh issuance of the exact same underlying signed bootstrap/dataset authorization pair (would only be possible if ADR-0141's own one-use root-pis WORM/reserve key did not already prevent a second root-pis row for that pair — cross-check against ADR-0141, not re-litigated here)
matrix.expected_outcome: second INSERT collides on the reserve_uses (kind,signed_id) PRIMARY KEY -> sqlite3.IntegrityError -> caught and re-raised, mirroring _SyntheticRootPisIssuer.issue (trust.py:8437-8440); no second dynamic authority instance is ever registered in _P4_ISSUED for a colliding signed_id

cases: root_pis_ref and dataset_g1_ref swapped (kind mismatch, e.g. a G1 grant ref supplied where root_pis_ref is expected)
dataset_g1_ref and dataset_g2_ref swapped (role confusion, G1 bytes supplied as G2)
root_pis_ref pointing at a byte-identical-looking but wrong-schema artifact (e.g. issuance-basis/v2 instead of published-input-set/v2)
duplicate ref (same ref used for two of the three fields)
matrix.expected_outcome: find(kind, digest) requires exactly one match of the EXACT kind; a swapped/wrong-kind ref fails the kind-specific lookup (_hs_refuse('P4 closure requires one exact referenced artifact')) before any dependency walk completes
matrix.forbidden_effect: accepting a structurally-valid-looking ref of the wrong kind/role because only sha256 was checked, or because two closed refs happened to collide in a projection

cases: pce for input_id=raw_event_dataset carrying a planned_entry_sha256 whose preimage names source_roster's contract_sha256 (entry swap)
pce carrying a contract_sha256 that matches neither PIS entry (foreign/invented digest)
two pce rows both bound to the same PIS entry (missing the second entry, duplicate binding)
matrix.expected_outcome: planned_entry_sha256 must equal _digest(_hs_canonical_bytes({"root_pis_entry_input_id": <input_id>, "root_pis_contract_sha256": <that SAME entry's own contract_sha256>})) recomputed from the resolver's own held PIS entries, not trusted from the pce row; any mismatch refuses
matrix.forbidden_effect: accepting a pce row whose input_id/contract_sha256 pairing does not match one specific PIS entry 1:1; accepting fewer or more than exactly 2 pce rows

matrix.family: revocation or clock advance observed mid-admission
cases: revocation token added to reserve_revoked between graph.snapshot() and a later graph.resolve() call using that token
trusted-host _advance_clock() call lands between the before-vector read and the after-vector read inside a single snapshot()/resolve() call

revocation/clock change lands between commit_p4_batch's first _P4_SNAPSHOT_INTEGRITY check (trust.py:5271) and its second one inside the try block (trust.py:5292), i.e. across the ledger's own two-phase re-check
matrix.expected_outcome: the graph's own before/after _vector() fence refuses on any mismatch ('dynamic root snapshot freshness changed' / 'dynamic root resolve freshness changed'); commit_p4_batch's own re-checks (_check(), _P4_REQUEST_CHECK, _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION re-call) catch a change that slips past a single resolver call
matrix.forbidden_effect: a CAPTURED batch committing with any artifact bytes or admission closure proven against a since-changed revocation/clock state

matrix.family: crash/ambiguous COMMIT during the one-shot dynamic-p4-authority reserve transition
cases: process crash after the INSERT ... RESERVED statement but before the UPDATE ... ISSUED statement, both inside the SAME BEGIN IMMEDIATE (per the pinned reserve_row_pin.transition shape, both statements are in one transaction — so this case can only leave either NO row (ROLLBACK/crash before COMMIT) or a fully ISSUED row (crash after COMMIT); it cannot leave a bare RESERVED row from THIS transaction alone)
ambiguous COMMIT result (connection.execute('COMMIT') raises or the process dies while the OS/driver has not confirmed) followed by a retry of the SAME construction call

quarantine path: reserve COMMIT succeeds but a LATER step in the broker (constructing the resolver/terminal objects, or whatever follows) raises — per the reserve-first ordering pinned above, this cannot leave the ROW itself broken, but the AUTHORITY was never fully constructed/returned
matrix.expected_outcome: on retry, a fresh SELECT sees the row already ISSUED (if the crashed transaction actually committed) or absent (if it rolled back); either way the retry's own INSERT either collides (IntegrityError, row already ISSUED) or proceeds cleanly (row absent) — never a partial/ambiguous RESERVED-only state left visible from a fully-local single-transaction insert+update. A failure AFTER a successful reserve COMMIT but before the broker returns successfully must be handled by an explicit quarantine call (not specified by ADR text — Phase 0 deliverable, see class_function_inventory._development_dynamic_p4_broker)
matrix.forbidden_effect: a second successful construction attempt after an ambiguous/crashed first attempt that DID commit; a resolver/authority object returned to a caller when the underlying reserve row never reached ISSUED

matrix.family: run-identity reuse across the legacy and dynamic authority instances
cases: the SAME consumer_run_identity string used to capture through the legacy authority AND the dynamic authority
a run_identity that is the PRODUCER run on the legacy authority's stream, submitted as the CONSUMER run on the dynamic authority (cross-instance producer/consumer confusion)
a run_identity already used in a legacy CAPTURED_V1 entry on one ledger, replayed as a P4 consumer run on the OTHER ledger
matrix.expected_outcome: per Decision point 8: run-identity exclusivity is inherited unchanged from _validate_capture_request/commit_p4_batch and is enforced PER-INSTANCE (each authority has its own _stream_pin/_sessions; each ledger has its own _root/_p4_entries()); the ADR adds NO cross-instance run-identity check and does not claim one — reusing the same run_identity string across the two independent authority instances is NOT refused by anything this ADR adds, and is explicitly out of scope per Decision point 8 ('no cross-instance run-identity check is added or required by this slice')
matrix.forbidden_effect: NONE claimed by this ADR for the cross-instance case — this row exists to make explicit, for the independent skeptic, that cross-instance run-identity reuse is a DELIBERATE non-goal, not an oversight; if the skeptic disagrees this needs a fresh reviewed decision, not a silent Phase-0 fix

matrix.family: concurrent construction attempts (two threads/processes racing the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE)
cases: two processes call _development_dynamic_p4_broker(issuer) for the SAME issuer at the same instant; both read the root-pis row as ISSUED, both attempt BEGIN IMMEDIATE

IF the reserve spend happens AFTER resolver/terminal construction (the ordering explicitly NOT frozen by the ADR, flagged above): two full _DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver instances get built from the SAME memoized graph object (issuer.graph() is idempotent/memoized, trust.py:8481-8483) before either reserve spend resolves; only one call's INSERT wins, the other's IntegrityError refuses — but by then TWO live resolver objects exist pointing at ONE graph instance whose `_snapshot` is a single mutable slot (trust.py:8970,8978) overwritten by whichever resolver calls graph.snapshot() LAST

two THREADS in one process holding references to both resolver objects; thread A calls resolverA.snapshot() (sets graph._snapshot = tokenA), thread B calls resolverB.snapshot() (overwrites graph._snapshot = tokenB), thread A then calls resolverA.resolve(tokenA, ref) — graph.resolve requires `snapshot is self._snapshot`, so tokenA now fails with 'exact issued dynamic root snapshot required' even though tokenA was validly issued by the SAME graph a moment earlier

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.summary: _p4_fixed_integrity() (legacy-only dispatch-integrity self-check) runs unconditionally inside _p4_snapshot_integrity before the type dispatch; no analogous self-check is specified for the new dynamic branch's own pins (_dynamic_p4_close_admission identity, dynamic clock/revocations method identity, dynamic terminal verifier method identity). This is an asymmetry between the two branches' resistance to in-process tampering, even though both are out-of-scope for the EXTERNAL threat model per implementation-workflow.md point 4. This matrix recommends adding an analogous _p4_dynamic_fixed_integrity() called from the new elif branch; the independent skeptic should confirm this is required (or explicitly accept the asymmetry) rather than the implementer silently deciding it.

The ADR's Decision point 2 says the resolver performs 'the identical before-proof/_prove()/after-proof vector fence that NonAuthorizingDynamicRootGraph.resolve already performs internally' on every snapshot()/_checked_resolve() call. Since graph.snapshot()/graph.resolve() ALREADY perform this exact fence internally (trust.py:8947-9015), it is ambiguous whether the resolver is meant to (a) simply delegate to graph.snapshot()/resolve() and rely entirely on their existing fence (no new code, 'identical' just describes the inherited behavior), or (b) additionally perform its OWN separate before/after vector read as defense-in-depth on top of the graph's. Phase 0 must pin which; (a) is simpler and avoids the two-live-resolver race surfaced in matrix row 11 being made worse by extra unguarded reads, but (b) is what a literal reading of 'performs the identical... fence' suggests. This matrix recommends (a).

Reserve-spend ordering inside _development_dynamic_p4_broker (before vs. after resolver/terminal construction) is not frozen by the ADR text. This matrix's matrix rows 9 and 11 both depend on pinning RESERVE-FIRST; the independent skeptic should treat this as a required Phase 0 pin, not a stylistic choice, given the concrete two-live-resolver race in row 11.
